data.title: Contact Energy CFO boosts personal stake in company shares
data.description:
Contact Energy Limited ( (NZ:CEN) ) has provided an announcement.

Contact Energy’s chief financial officer, Matthew James Forbes, has increased his personal holding of the company’s ordinary shares through an on-market purchase, according to a disclosure filed with the NZX. Forbes acquired 2,300 shares at NZ$8.65 each, lifting his directly held stake to 13,074.08 ordinary shares, while his entitlement under the employee share ownership plan remains unchanged at 356 shares.

The transaction, completed on 2 September 2026, forms part of ongoing disclosure obligations under New Zealand’s Financial Markets Conduct Act and underscores transparency around insider holdings at the utility. The update may be read by investors as a signal of executive confidence in Contact Energy’s prospects, while reinforcing regulatory compliance and governance standards for senior management trading activity.

data.title: Anton Oilfield Gains Iraq Crude Sales Role, Expands Full-Chain Services
data.description:
The latest update is out from Anton Oilfield Services Group ( (HK:3337) ).

Anton Oilfield Services Group has secured approval from Iraq’s Ministry of Oil to enter a long-term cooperation with the State Oil Marketing Company, gaining crude oil sales qualification and becoming a designated partner for crude oil export sales. The group obtained lifting rights for self-operated oilfields of Iraq’s national oil company and general long-term sales cooperation status, positioning it as a lifting and settlement service provider that links crude oil sales with service providers and buyers.

Under the agreement, Anton will coordinate lifting arrangements, facilitate resource monetisation and support settlement needs across Iraq’s oil and gas ecosystem, while helping SOMO expand its market share. The new crude-linked settlement channel is described as an innovative business model that extends Anton’s service chain into oil and gas commercialisation support, strengthens ties with Iraqi authorities and enhances the company’s resilience, making it the only Chinese independent energy firm in Iraq with combined capabilities in technical services, resource development and crude oil sales.

data.title: Sunshine Oilsands to Issue Discounted Shares to Settle Debt
data.description:
Sunshine Oilsands ( (HK:2012) ) has shared an update.

Sunshine Oilsands has agreed to issue new shares under its existing general mandate to settle outstanding debts owed to certain creditors, converting liabilities into equity. The shares will be issued at HK$0.171, a discount to recent market prices, and will account for about 13.85% of current share capital, or 12.16% of the enlarged capital base once the transaction closes.

The issuance, which does not require additional shareholder approval, is intended to strengthen the company’s balance sheet by reducing debt obligations but will dilute existing shareholders’ stakes. Completion remains subject to conditions in the settlement agreement, and the company has warned investors to exercise caution, underscoring some execution risk and potential volatility around the stock as the deal proceeds.

data.title: China Environmental Technology Reaches Settlement Over Disputed Convertible Bonds
data.description:
China Environmental Technology Holdings Limited ( (HK:0646) ) has shared an announcement.

China Environmental Technology Holdings has settled a long-running dispute over its 2021 convertible bonds by signing a Deed of Settlement with creditor Sure Fast. The agreement follows prior court rulings affirming the validity and enforceability of the bond-related agreements, bringing greater clarity to the company’s financial obligations.

Under the Deed, the company will pay a final settlement sum of US$11.29 million plus interest in three instalments through the end of 2027. In return, Sure Fast has agreed not to pursue winding-up petitions, new legal actions, or enforcement of the Hong Kong High Court judgment, unless the company defaults, reducing immediate legal and insolvency risks for shareholders and creditors.
